newsitem.title: USA: Hartford mayor says 50-50 chance Whalers to stay.
newsitem.headline: Hartford mayor says 50-50 chance Whalers to stay.

text.p: Hartford Mayor Mike Peters said Thursday there was a 50-50 chance that a new arena will be built for the National Hockey League's Hartford Whalers.
The issue should be settled in about three weeks, Peters told Reuters in an interview.
The Whalers said last month that the state must build a new arena, costing as much as $240 million in taxpayers' money, if it wants the team to stay in Connecticut.
But the figure has now been whittled down to about $160 million and the Whalers have agreed to kick in some money, said Peters.
"Fifty-fifty," Peters said when asked about the chances of keeping the team.
City officials are working closely with Governor John Rowland to find ways to keep the team, said Peters.
He said the governor's office was now "crunching numbers" to come up with an affordable plan to build an arena in Hartford.
"If the numbers don't work, they don't work, and then we have to stand back and say, What do we do?" said Peters.
The Whalers and the state were "not far apart (on the issue) at all, contrary to what's been written in some of our newspapers," said Peters.
"They like each other. They're both businessmen. The governor is a businessman, and so is (team owner Peter) Karmanos."
"I think we're going to be OK," said Peters.
The Whalers feel the Civic Center is inadequate partly because the luxury boxes are too high up and do not generate enough money, said Peters.
The seating capacity of about 14,000 was too small for the team, which wants 18,000 capacity, he said. Peters said it
would be economically "devastating" for Hartford if the Whalers chose to leave.
"It would hurt," he said. "Forty or 45 games a year downtown on average, (and) 12,500 or 13,000 people a game."
He said Connecticut fans traditionally had a love-hate relationship with the team, depending on the Whalers' ownership and performance over the years.
"This team has not been one of the more outstanding teams in the NHL. But they have good ownership now, and you can see it in the way they're playing, and the fans are coming back."
The Whalers are currently in third place in the Northeast division of the NHL's Eastern conference.

"The fans are very adamant," said Peters. "They want this team to stay here. I hear it every day. But it's very important (to keep the Whalers), not just for the city of Hartford, but for the state of Connecticut."
--Matthew Lewis, Hartford newsroom (860) 727-0224
